hypothesis: A host-visible coherent private-Turnip allocation exported as an opaque FD can be mapped directly by the glibc client, eliminating eligible E077 mirror copies.

sequence: write deterministic pattern through source Vulkan mapping
POSIX mmap the FD and verify the source pattern
write a second pattern through the raw FD mapping
import the same allocation into a second Vulkan device and verify it
write a third pattern through the destination Vulkan mapping
verify the third pattern through the still-live raw FD mapping
implementation.noncoherent_memory: fail closed; this bounded gate requires HOST_COHERENT

recall.query: Turnip KGSL Vulkan external memory opaque fd mmap CPU host visible allocation direct shared mapped memory glibc Bionic bridge
recall.reuse: E138 reuses E035's real opaque-FD export/import bootstrap and memory-type selection. It adds only the previously unproven raw mmap and bidirectional CPU visibility checks behind an explicit mode.

next_gate: Build the E138 Bionic probe on the tablet and run it against the unchanged private Turnip loader. Host memfd success is not evidence that KGSL's exported FD is mmapable.
claim_boundary: This proves the bounded test and fake-driver semantics only. It does not prove private-Turnip raw mapping, cross-libc FD transport, mirror removal, a rendered frame, or an FPS improvement.
